title: Search basics (grep and ripgrep)
intro: Work from home. You'll be searching across real system directories: **`/var/log`**, **`/etc`**, and **`/usr/local/share`**. Use **`grep`** for questions 1–8 unless noted.

questions.prompt: The system auth log at `/var/log/auth.log` records SSH and sudo activity. How many lines in that file contain the word `Failed`?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
grep -c 'Failed' /var/log/auth.log
```

One entry records a failed password attempt.

questions.prompt: In `/var/log/auth.log`, find the line that records a failed login. What username was targeted?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
grep 'Failed' /var/log/auth.log
```

The line reads `Failed password for invalid user admin` — the targeted account is **admin**.

questions.prompt: The application log at `/var/log/course/app.log` records events with severity levels `INFO`, `WARN`, and `ERROR`. How many lines are NOT at `INFO` level?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
grep -vc 'INFO' /var/log/course/app.log
```

The file has one `ERROR` and one `WARN` entry — two non-`INFO` lines.

questions.prompt: Search `/etc/course-lab/` (non-recursively, `*.conf` files only) for files that contain the key `API_KEY`. How many such files are there?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
grep -l 'API_KEY' /etc/course-lab/*.conf | wc -l
```

Only `app.conf` has the `.conf` extension — `app.conf.old` does not match `*.conf`.

questions.prompt: One file inside `/etc/course-lab/` contains the word `staging`. Search the directory (non-recursively) across all files. What is the **filename** of the match (no path prefix)?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
grep -l 'staging' /etc/course-lab/* | xargs -n1 basename
```

The old config `app.conf.old` records `environment=staging`.

questions.prompt: Search `/var/log/course/archive/` recursively and case-insensitively for lines that contain the word `fail`. How many matching lines are there in total across all files?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
grep -ri 'fail' /var/log/course/archive/ | wc -l
```

`build.log` has two matching lines: `fail deploy` and `fail backup`. The rotated `app.log.1` has none.

questions.prompt: Inside `/usr/local/share/course/docs/` (search recursively), find all `.txt` files that contain a version string in the form `X.Y.Z` (three integers separated by dots). Print the full path of each matching file, one per line.
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
grep -rlE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' /usr/local/share/course/docs/ --include='*.txt'
```

Only `versions.txt` contains version strings like `1.2.3` and `v2.10.0`.

questions.prompt: Search `/usr/local/share/course/docs/` recursively for any file containing `SECRET`. What is the value assigned to `SECRET` (everything after the `=`)?

The `/etc/course-lab/` directory contains a hidden subdirectory. Search that entire tree recursively (including hidden directories) for any line matching the pattern `MODULE[0-9][0-9]_FLAG=`. What is the full flag value (everything after `=`)?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
grep -r 'MODULE[0-9][0-9]_FLAG=' /etc/course-lab/
```

The flag is stored in `/etc/course-lab/.cache/flag`. Standard recursive `grep` follows hidden directories — just make sure you start at the right root.

questions.prompt: The auth log records one sudo invocation. Find the `COMMAND=` field in that line and extract just the command path (the value after `COMMAND=`).
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
grep 'sudo' /var/log/auth.log | grep -oP 'COMMAND=\K\S+'
```

Or with `awk`:
```bash
grep 'sudo' /var/log/auth.log | awk -F'COMMAND=' '{print $2}'
```

summaryMarkdown:
## Learning outcomes
- Choose fixed-string vs regex search; recursive directory search with sensible exclusions.
- Use line vs binary mode; handle matches in binary files safely (`-I`, `-a`).
- Compare BSD `grep` (macOS) with GNU `grep` and **ripgrep** (`rg`) for daily development search.

## Scope

**In scope:** CLI search in files and stdin. **Out of scope:** full PCRE / advanced **`grep` + `rg`** curriculum (**11**); codebase semantic search (LSP/ctags) as a sidebar only.

## Concept outline

1. **`grep` flags** — `-r`, `-R` (follow symlinks caution), `-n`, `-H`, `-h`, `-l`, `-L`, `-c`, `-o`, `-E`, `-F`, `-w`, `-x`.
2. **Binary files** — `-I` skip, `-a` treat as text; why `grep` may say “Binary file matches”.
3. **Performance** — `LANG=C` / `LC_ALL=C`; `grep -F` for literals.
4. **`rg` (ripgrep)** — treat as the default recursive searcher in repos: `.gitignore` / `.rgignore` / `.ignore` defaults, `-S` / `--smart-case`, `-uuu` unrestricted, `-t` / `-T` file types, `-g` / `--glob`, `--hidden`, `--json` for tooling, **`--pcre2`** vs default Rust regex (full PCRE story in **11**).
5. **Git-aware search** — `git grep` for committed tree vs working tree; integrates with revision ranges.

## Tooling and alternatives

| Task | Primary | Alternatives |
|------|---------|----------------|
| Recursive regex search | `grep -rE` | `rg` (default choice in repos), `ag` / `ack` (legacy), `ugrep` (`ug`) with SIMD and optional GPU path. |
| Fixed-string search | `grep -F` | `rg -F`, `fgrep` compatibility name. |
| Search in git tree | `git grep` | `rg` with path; `git grep` wins for `git log -S` style workflows (different command). |
| Count per file | `grep -c` | `rg --count`, `rg --count-matches`. |
| Filter lines (stdin) | `grep` | `rg` stdin; `awk /re/`; `sed -n '/re/p'`. |
